glossary.Immune-mediated: Caused by the body's own immune system acting abnormally.
glossary.Scale: Flakes of dead skin on the surface of a lesion.
glossary.Plaques: Raised, flat-topped skin lesions more than about 1 cm across.
glossary.Papular: Made of small raised spots (papules) under 1 cm.
glossary.Monomorphic: All the lesions look the same.
glossary.Psoriatic: Caused by or relating to psoriasis.
glossary.Streptococcal: Caused by Streptococcus bacteria, often a sore throat in guttate psoriasis.
glossary.Cardiovascular disease: Disease of the heart and blood vessels, such as heart attack and stroke.
glossary.Aspirin: An antiplatelet and anti-inflammatory drug that can trigger psoriasis flares.
glossary.Propranolol: A non-selective beta-blocker that can trigger psoriasis flares.
glossary.Steroid withdrawal: Stopping steroids, especially suddenly, which can cause a rebound flare of psoriasis.
glossary.Biopsy: Taking a small piece of tissue to look at under a microscope.
glossary.Topical corticosteroid: A steroid cream or ointment applied to the skin to reduce inflammation.
glossary.Potent: A strong grade of topical steroid, such as betamethasone.
glossary.Betamethasone valerate: A potent topical steroid, often used as a scalp application.
glossary.Emollient: A moisturiser that softens and soothes dry skin.
glossary.Systemic: Acting on the whole body, for example tablets or injections rather than creams.
glossary.Anti-folate: A drug that blocks folate use, slowing division of rapidly dividing cells; methotrexate is one.
glossary.Retinoid: A vitamin A derivative; acitretin is an oral retinoid that is highly teratogenic.
glossary.Contraindicated: Should not be used because of a risk of harm.
glossary.Mucous membranes: The moist linings of the mouth, nose and eyes.
glossary.Photochemotherapy: Light treatment combined with a light-sensitising drug, as in PUVA.
glossary.Squamous cell carcinoma: A skin cancer arising from keratinocytes, increased after PUVA.
glossary.IL-12: Interleukin-12, a cytokine that drives Th1 responses; shares the p40 subunit with IL-23.
glossary.p40 subunit: The protein piece shared by IL-12 and IL-23 that ustekinumab binds.
glossary.Interleukin: A signalling protein (cytokine) that immune cells use to talk to each other.
glossary.T-cell: A white blood cell that directs and carries out cell-mediated immunity.
glossary.Autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.Suprapapillary epidermis: The thin layer of epidermis lying over the dermal papillae.
glossary.Epidermis: The outer layer of the skin, made mostly of keratinocytes.
glossary.Dermal: Relating to the dermis, the layer of skin beneath the epidermis.
glossary.Antigens: Molecules that the immune system recognises and responds to.
glossary.Low-grade inflammation: Mild but long-lasting inflammation throughout the body.
glossary.Turnover: The time taken for new skin cells to replace old ones.
